supported_claims.text: 我, “I” or “me,” began as a picture of a long-handled weapon or tool. The written sign was borrowed for its sound to write the pronoun. Its modern resemblance to a hand beside a weapon does not mean that “defending oneself” explains the origin of the word “I.”
A pictorial sign for an implement was reused for a pronoun through sound. The borrowing explains the current use; the older drawing explains the shape.

disagreements.text: The precise implement is disputed. It is reasonable to describe the overall object picture and the pronoun borrowing while leaving the exact weapon or tool unidentified.
